long_biography.plain_text:
Dario Gianandrea Ferrari entered cosmetics after advertising work in London and sales experience with a Swiss skincare brand owned by his mother. In 1972, he acquired a small Italian lipstick producer and built the enterprise that became Intercos. His model combined contract manufacturing with product development, marketing insight and sustained investment in research.

Intercos expanded from colour cosmetics into skincare, hair and body care, supported by international laboratories and factories. Ferrari remains the listed group's controlling shareholder through Dafe holding companies and serves as executive chairman. The company separately names Renato Semerari as chief executive, so Ferrari's present role is best understood as founder control, board leadership and strategic direction rather than sole operational management.
